title: Spread the Routers Out
statement:
A long street has `n` poles at distinct positions along it. You must mount `k` routers on `k` different poles. You want the routers to interfere as little as possible, so you maximise the smallest distance between any two routers. Find that largest possible smallest distance.

## Input
The first line contains `n` and `k`. The second line contains `n` distinct integers, the positions of the poles (not necessarily sorted).

## Output
Print the largest value `d` such that `k` routers can be placed on poles with every two routers at least `d` apart.

## Constraints
- `2 <= k <= n <= 100000`
- `0 <= position <= 10^9`
